conventions: All monetary columns are in INR.
REFUND transactions carry a NEGATIVE gross_amount, total_charged and net_amount, so SUM(net_amount) is already true net revenue - never filter refunds out unless asked.
FAILED transactions have fee = 0, net_amount = 0 and settlement_date IS NULL.
Only transactions with status = 'SETTLED' roll up into SETTLEMENTS and the LEDGER.

tables.name: TRANSACTIONS
tables.grain: One row per card transaction captured at a terminal.
tables.description: Card payment transactions for a small merchant across three acquiring providers and five terminals. Covers sales and refunds, the fee charged by the acquirer, and whether the money has been settled yet. This is the primary revenue table.

columns.name: transaction_id
columns.description: Primary key, e.g. TXN000123.

columns.name: direction
columns.description: 'SALE' or 'REFUND'. REFUND rows have negative amounts.

columns.name: txn_datetime
columns.description: When the card was tapped/swiped.

columns.name: value_date
columns.description: Calendar date of the transaction. Use this for daily/monthly grouping.

columns.name: provider
columns.description: Acquiring provider: RAZORPAY, PINELABS or PAYTM.

columns.name: terminal_id
columns.description: Card machine that captured the payment. Joins to CARD_MACHINE_ACCOUNTS.terminal_id.

columns.name: merchant_id
columns.description: Merchant account the terminal belongs to.

columns.name: card_type
columns.description: Card network: VISA, MASTERCARD or RUPAY.

columns.name: card_last4
columns.description: Last four digits of the card.

columns.name: auth_code
columns.description: Issuer authorisation code.

columns.name: category
columns.description: Sales category: DINE_IN, TAKEAWAY, DELIVERY, MERCHANDISE or CATERING.

columns.name: gross_amount
columns.description: Bill amount before tip. Negative for refunds.

columns.name: tip
columns.description: Tip added at the terminal. Only ever non-zero for DINE_IN sales.

columns.name: total_charged
columns.description: gross_amount + tip. The amount actually charged to the card.

columns.name: fee
columns.description: Acquirer processing fee, always positive, 0 when the transaction FAILED. This is a cost to the merchant.

columns.name: net_amount
columns.description: total_charged - fee. The merchant's net receipt. SUM this for net revenue.

columns.name: currency
columns.description: Always 'INR'.

columns.name: status
columns.description: 'SETTLED', 'PENDING' or 'FAILED'.

columns.name: settlement_date
columns.description: Date the payout batch landed. NULL unless status = 'SETTLED'.

columns.name: notes
columns.description: Free-text note; populated for failed, pending and refund rows.

relationships: TRANSACTIONS.transaction_id <- DISPUTES.orig_txn_id (a dispute is raised against one transaction)
common_metrics: net revenue = SUM(net_amount)
gross sales = SUM(total_charged) WHERE direction = 'SALE'
total fees paid = SUM(fee)
effective fee rate = SUM(fee) / SUM(ABS(total_charged))
failure rate = COUNT_IF(status = 'FAILED') / COUNT(*)
refund rate = SUM(ABS(total_charged)) FILTER on direction='REFUND' / SUM(total_charged) FILTER on direction='SALE'
average ticket size = AVG(total_charged) WHERE direction = 'SALE'
example_questions: What is our net revenue by provider this year?
Which sales category brings in the most money?
How much have we paid in card processing fees per month?
What is our transaction failure rate by terminal?

tables.name: DISPUTES
tables.grain: One row per cardholder dispute (chargeback) raised against a transaction.
tables.description: Chargebacks and disputes raised by cardholders. Tracks why the dispute was raised, the deadline to respond, whether the merchant submitted evidence, the outcome, and how much money was clawed back or recovered. Use this for chargeback performance, win rates and dispute losses.

columns.name: dispute_id
columns.description: Primary key, e.g. DSP00012.

columns.name: orig_txn_id
columns.description: Foreign key to TRANSACTIONS.transaction_id - the disputed transaction.

columns.name: date_raised
columns.description: Date the cardholder raised the dispute. Use this for time grouping.

columns.name: response_deadline
columns.description: Date by which the merchant must submit evidence (date_raised + 14 days).

columns.name: date_resolved
columns.description: Date the dispute was decided. NULL while outcome = 'PENDING'.

columns.name: provider
columns.description: Acquiring provider handling the dispute.

columns.name: terminal_id
columns.description: Terminal where the disputed transaction happened.

columns.name: merchant_id
columns.description: Merchant account.

columns.name: card_type
columns.description: Card network of the disputed transaction.

columns.name: card_last4
columns.description: Last four digits of the disputed card.

columns.name: dispute_reason
columns.description: One of FRAUD_UNAUTHORISED, PRODUCT_NOT_RECEIVED, DUPLICATE_CHARGE, INCORRECT_AMOUNT, SERVICE_QUALITY.

columns.name: description
columns.description: Narrative of the cardholder's claim.

columns.name: disputed_amount
columns.description: Amount under dispute, equal to the original transaction's total_charged.

columns.name: chargeback_fee
columns.description: Flat fee the provider charges per chargeback, from FEE_SCHEDULE.

columns.name: outcome
columns.description: 'WON' (merchant kept the money), 'LOST' (cardholder kept the money) or 'PENDING'.

columns.name: evidence_provided
columns.description: TRUE if the merchant submitted supporting evidence. Strongly correlated with winning.

columns.name: cb_debited
columns.description: TRUE if the provider has already debited the disputed amount.

columns.name: amount_recovered
columns.description: Amount returned to the merchant; equals disputed_amount when outcome = 'WON', otherwise 0.

columns.name: notes
columns.description: Resolution note.

common_metrics: dispute win rate = COUNT_IF(outcome = 'WON') / COUNT_IF(outcome <> 'PENDING')
net chargeback loss = SUM(disputed_amount - amount_recovered)
total chargeback fees = SUM(chargeback_fee)
open disputes = COUNT_IF(outcome = 'PENDING')
overdue disputes = COUNT_IF(outcome = 'PENDING' AND response_deadline < CURRENT_DATE())
days to resolve = AVG(DATEDIFF('day', date_raised, date_resolved))
dispute rate = COUNT(*) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM TRANSACTIONS)
example_questions: Which disputes are we most likely to lose?
What is our chargeback win rate by provider?
How much have we lost to chargebacks this year?
Does providing evidence actually improve our win rate?

tables.name: SETTLEMENTS
tables.grain: One row per payout batch (provider + terminal + settlement_date).
tables.description: Money actually paid out to the merchant's bank account. Each row aggregates all settled transactions for one terminal on one settlement date. Use this for payout reliability, pending payouts and cash-in timing.

columns.name: settlement_id
columns.description: Primary key, e.g. STL00042.

columns.name: provider
columns.description: Provider making the payout.

columns.name: terminal_id
columns.description: Terminal whose takings are in this batch.

columns.name: merchant_id
columns.description: Merchant account receiving the payout.

columns.name: settlement_date
columns.description: Date the batch was paid out. Use this for time grouping.

columns.name: batch_txn_count
columns.description: Number of transactions in the batch.

columns.name: gross_amount
columns.description: Sum of total_charged for the batch.

columns.name: total_fees
columns.description: Sum of acquirer fees deducted from the batch.

columns.name: net_settled_amount
columns.description: gross_amount - total_fees. What actually hit the bank.

columns.name: bank_account
columns.description: Masked destination bank account.

columns.name: payout_reference
columns.description: Provider's payout reference string.

columns.name: status
columns.description: 'PAID' or 'PENDING'. PENDING means the payout has not landed yet.

relationships: SETTLEMENTS is derived from TRANSACTIONS WHERE status = 'SETTLED', grouped by provider, terminal_id, merchant_id, settlement_date
common_metrics: total settled = SUM(net_settled_amount)
pending payout value = SUM(net_settled_amount) WHERE status = 'PENDING'
pending payout count = COUNT_IF(status = 'PENDING')
average batch size = AVG(batch_txn_count)
fee drag per batch = SUM(total_fees) / SUM(gross_amount)
settlement reliability = COUNT_IF(status = 'PAID') / COUNT(*)
example_questions: Which settlement batches are still pending?
How much is owed to us in unpaid payouts?
What is the average payout size by provider?
Show settled amount per month.

tables.name: LEDGER
tables.description: Simplified double-entry general ledger derived from transactions, disputes and settlements. Total debits equal total credits. Use this to trace the accounting impact of any business event, and to chart account balances over time.

columns.name: ledger_entry_id
columns.description: Primary key, e.g. GL0000123.

columns.name: entry_date
columns.description: Posting date. Use this for time grouping.

columns.name: account_code
columns.description: Account code: '1010' Bank Account, '1200' Card Receivable, '4000' Sales Revenue, '5100' Card Processing Fees, '5200' Chargeback Losses.

columns.name: account_name
columns.description: Human-readable account name matching account_code.

columns.name: debit
columns.description: Debit amount, 0 if this posting is a credit.

columns.name: credit
columns.description: Credit amount, 0 if this posting is a debit.

columns.name: source_type
columns.description: What generated the posting: 'TRANSACTION', 'DISPUTE' or 'SETTLEMENT'.

columns.name: source_id
columns.description: The id of the originating row. Join to TRANSACTIONS.transaction_id, DISPUTES.dispute_id or SETTLEMENTS.settlement_id depending on source_type.

columns.name: description
columns.description: Narrative for the posting.

columns.name: running_balance
columns.description: Cumulative (debit - credit) FOR THAT ACCOUNT ordered by entry_date. To chart a balance trend you MUST filter to a single account_code, e.g. WHERE account_code = '1010'.

common_metrics: bank balance trend = SELECT entry_date, MAX(running_balance) FROM LEDGER WHERE account_code = '1010' GROUP BY entry_date ORDER BY entry_date
total processing fee expense = SUM(debit) WHERE account_code = '5100'
total chargeback loss expense = SUM(debit) WHERE account_code = '5200'
revenue recognised = SUM(credit) - SUM(debit) WHERE account_code = '4000'
outstanding receivable = SUM(debit) - SUM(credit) WHERE account_code = '1200'
ledger is balanced when SUM(debit) = SUM(credit)
example_questions: Show me the bank account balance trend since April.
What was the ledger impact of disputes lost in May?
How much sits in card receivable right now?
Break down our expense accounts by month.

tables.name: CARD_MACHINE_ACCOUNTS
tables.description: Reference table describing each physical card machine the merchant operates: which provider supplied it, its contract dates and rates, whether it is still active, and which bank it settles into.

columns.name: provider
columns.description: Acquiring provider that supplied the terminal.

columns.name: merchant_id
columns.description: Merchant account the terminal is registered under.

columns.name: terminal_id
columns.description: Primary key, e.g. TERM-RZP-01.

columns.name: status
columns.description: 'ACTIVE' or 'INACTIVE'. One terminal (TERM-PIN-02) is INACTIVE.

columns.name: contract_start
columns.description: Contract start date.

columns.name: contract_end
columns.description: Contract end date - useful for finding contracts expiring soon.

columns.name: transaction_fee
columns.description: Headline contracted per-transaction rate as a decimal, e.g. 0.0180 = 1.80%.

columns.name: monthly_fee
columns.description: Fixed monthly rental for the machine.

columns.name: settlement_bank
columns.description: Bank the terminal settles into.

columns.name: account_manager_contact
columns.description: Provider-side contact email.

common_metrics: active terminals = COUNT_IF(status = 'ACTIVE')
total monthly rental = SUM(monthly_fee) WHERE status = 'ACTIVE'
contracts expiring within 180 days = COUNT_IF(contract_end < DATEADD('day', 180, CURRENT_DATE()))
example_questions: Which terminals are inactive?
What do we pay in monthly machine rental?
Which contracts expire in the next six months?

tables.name: FEE_SCHEDULE
tables.grain: One row per provider + card network combination.
tables.description: Contracted rate card. Defines the per-transaction rate, monthly fee, flat chargeback fee and foreign-exchange surcharge for each provider and card network. Use this to compare providers on price or to check whether transactions were charged correctly.

columns.name: provider
columns.description: RAZORPAY, PINELABS or PAYTM.

columns.name: card_type
columns.description: VISA, MASTERCARD or RUPAY.

columns.name: transaction_fee
columns.description: Per-transaction rate as a decimal, e.g. 0.0195 = 1.95%. RUPAY is materially cheaper than VISA/MASTERCARD everywhere.

columns.name: monthly_fee
columns.description: Fixed monthly fee for the provider.

columns.name: chargeback_fee
columns.description: Flat fee charged per chargeback raised.

columns.name: fx_surcharge
columns.description: Additional rate applied to foreign cards. 0 for RUPAY.

common_metrics: cheapest provider per network = MIN(transaction_fee) GROUP BY card_type
rate spread = MAX(transaction_fee) - MIN(transaction_fee)
blended contracted rate = AVG(transaction_fee)
example_questions: Which provider charges us the most per transaction?
Compare RUPAY rates across providers.
What is the chargeback fee for each provider?
